title: Loyal Subjects of a Federal Republic
subtitle: Gonzales, DeWitt Colony · late September 1835

clocks.label: THE DEMAND
clocks.note: Ugartechea's patience. When it fills, Castañeda marches. It will fill.

clocks.label: THE WORD SPREADS
clocks.note: Neighbours who know and are coming. Players want this one full.

timeline.title: Everyone in.
items: Your person's name at the top of your screen
Two Words in your bar. Already yours.
Nothing to hold. It is all on the screen.

voice.speaker: NARRATOR
voice.text: Last time you became someone. Today that person finds out what the government wants from them. Take two Words. You will spend them before the bell.

orders: Do a job nobody asked you to do.
Find out one true number about this town.
Stand next to somebody and make their turn better.

shots.provenance: Map of the DeWitt Colony, 1831 · Texas General Land Office · public domain

voice.speaker: NARRATOR
voice.text: Gonzales sits on the Guadalupe, seventy miles east of Béxar. Four days by oxcart. Two by fast horse. Everything that happens today happens at that distance.

shots.provenance: Ugartechea to Ponton, 1835 · Texas State Library and Archives Commission

voice.speaker: UGARTECHEA
voice.text: Colonel Domingo de Ugartechea, commanding at Béxar, presents his compliments. The bronze cannon lent to your town for defence against the Comanche is the property of the government. You will return it. I await your answer.

voice.speaker: NARRATOR
voice.text: He is entitled to it. The cannon does belong to the government. Nothing about this demand is illegal, and every adult in Gonzales knows it.

timeline.teacherNote: Hand the Turtle Bayou Resolutions (handout 01) to the Schoolmaster. Have them read the operative passage aloud, then ask: who are they saying they're loyal to?

timeline.eyebrow: TURN 1 · THE LETTER ON THE TABLE · COUNCIL

voice.speaker: NARRATOR
voice.text: Ponton has the letter in his hand. A hundred people are in the square. The cannon is thirty feet away under a tarpaulin. Ugartechea wants an answer by the time his rider gets back. What do you do right now?

postings.title: THE ORCHARD
postings.line: Somebody has to get it in the ground before they come back for it.
postings.where: George Davis’s peach orchard, south-east past the path.

timeline.label: YOUR MOVE
timeline.instruction: Move. Choose. Keep going until the timer runs out.

voice.speaker: NARRATOR
voice.text: The rider is still watering his horse at the public trough, and he has not dismounted. Whatever this town says, he will carry it back word for word.

timeline.eyebrow: TURN 2 · SEVENTY MILES OF ROAD · MARCH

voice.speaker: NARRATOR
voice.text: Whatever this town decides, it cannot decide it alone. Mina is forty miles. San Felipe is eighty. There are maybe eighteen men in Gonzales who can hold a rifle. The nearest help is two days away and does not know anything is happening.

timeline.label: YOUR MOVE
timeline.instruction: Whatever you do, this town cannot do it alone. Seventy miles is seventy miles.

voice.speaker: NARRATOR
voice.text: Riders are on the road. Somewhere east of here a man you will never meet is being handed a letter about your town.

voice.speaker: NARRATOR
voice.text: A rider comes up the Béxar road at a walk. He is not a courier. He is a dragoon, and he is counting your houses.

timeline.label: YOUR MOVE
timeline.instruction: One unarmed man, doing something perfectly legal. Watch what this town does.

voice.speaker: NARRATOR
voice.text: The dragoon rides back the way he came, at the same walk, having counted everything he needed to count.

voice.speaker: NARRATOR
voice.text: Ponton's reply has to go tonight, and the cannon has to be somewhere. Both of those things are decided in the next ten minutes.

timeline.label: YOUR MOVE
timeline.instruction: The reply goes tonight and the cannon has to be somewhere. Both, in the next few minutes.

voice.speaker: NARRATOR
voice.text: THE DEMAND is full, or one segment from it. Say what that means out loud, and then say that Andrew Ponton really did stall, and that it really did work.

voice.speaker: NARRATOR
voice.text: Everyone is in the square. Do we return the cannon?

timeline.label: SPEAK
timeline.instruction: SPEAK costs a Word. The people who banked one now hold the floor.

timeline.question: Do we return the cannon?
timeline.instruction: Call it company by company. Delegate last.

voice.speaker: NARRATOR
voice.text: Whatever this town just voted, the cannon is still in the square and the young men of the Ranging Company have their own ideas about it. Sixteen-year-olds with a cannon do not take votes.

timeline.title: What you did.
items: Tap YOUR DAY. Every turn you took is in it.
Look at what the town has left.
The demand clock has not stopped.

voice.speaker: NARRATOR
voice.text: Look at your own record. Every turn you took, how it went, and what you found out. Then look at what this town has left, and how close the colonel is to marching.

blocks.head: Here's what was real today
blocks.body: The cannon. Ugartechea's demand. Andrew Ponton stalling. The Turtle Bayou Resolutions are a real document, and those men really did insist they were loyal Mexicans defending Mexico's own constitution. Zacatecas really happened, and Texans really did hear about it and understand exactly what it meant.

blocks.head: Here's what's contested
blocks.body: Historians still argue about why the colonists rebelled. Barker and Campbell say slavery mattered less than politics. Lack and Torget say the economy ran on cotton and slavery, and Mexico moving against it was structural. You need not pick. You do need to know serious people disagree.

blocks.head: Here's what I made up
blocks.body: Two things. The arguments made in this room today, and the parts of your character the record left blank — your Mark, and what you decided your person was like.

blocks.head: Your names are real. Your people are real.
blocks.body: The town, the cannon, the stalling, the forty days of food and the twelve rounds of powder are all real. That's the deal for the next five classes. I'll tell you every time which is which.

timeline.exitLine: Nobody in this room voted for a war. You're going to get one anyway. Ask yourself who actually decides these things.

recap: A colonel in Béxar wrote to Gonzales and asked for the town cannon back. He was entitled to it — the government had lent it, in writing, in 1831.
The town did not say no. It said the alcalde was away. Then it said the letter needed checking. It stalled for four days.
While it stalled, riders went out to the other colonies, and the cannon went into the ground in a peach orchard.
By the second of October there were a hundred and forty men in Gonzales, and a hundred Mexican dragoons across the river.
